newsitem.title: MEXICO: Sequined "Super Gay" lashes out at Mexican machos.
newsitem.headline: Sequined "Super Gay" lashes out at Mexican machos.

text.p: A masked campaigner for gay and lesbian rights symbolically closed down the headquarters of one of Mexico's top political parties on Monday for being too conservative and anti-homosexual.

"Super Gay," making his first outing in black, skin-tight shorts and boots with a flowing black cape covered with deep purple sequins, slapped a "Closed Down" sticker on the gates of the offices of the National Action Party (PAN).
"I am here to fight for the rights of gay citizens," Super Gay told reporters from behind his rainbow-coloured mask and flamboyant horned-rimmed glasses.

Officials and guards from the PAN made no attempt to stop the protest. The PAN is the leading right-of-centre party in Mexico and is seen as distinctly pro-church, promoting traditional family values.
"Super Gay" was accompanied by urban rights campaigner "Super Barrio" and environmentalist "Super Ecologista," two other masked rights fighters.

Mexico, often seen as the epitome of macho societies, has a long tradition of masked campaigners. They fight for the rights of poor and marginalized people, wearing wrestling-type costumes to appeal to lower classes.

Homosexuality is not covered by law in Mexico and thus not illegal, but it nonetheless is looked down upon in a heavily macho society where gays are less inclined to come out of the closet than in more liberal countries.
